Network.Institution.Name: Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais

Network.Objectives: The network was established in 2015 with the participation of researchers, undergraduate and graduate students aiming to evaluate species richness of butterflies (and other insects) in protected and altered areas in Minas Gerais state, Brazil. Network.Name: Long-term Ecological Research in Subtropical Atlantic Forests
Network.Institution.Name: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul
Network.Admin.Name: Sandra Cristina Müller
Network.Objectives: We believe that this project will expand ecological knowledge about the structure, function and dynamics of subtropical Atlantic forests, providing a robust basis for understanding the potential effects of the current climate crisis on ecosystem services provided by forests.
Network.Target: Dynamics forest| Structure forest | Ecosystem services
Network.Functioning.Doc.Reference: ForestPlots.net et. al 2021. Taking the pulse of Earth's tropical forests using networks of highly distributed plots
Network.Standard.Spatial.Structure: We maintain 13 sites with permanent plots across subtropical Atlantic Forests. 12 sites have 1 hectare as a reference of the permanent plot, but the sampling is done in 12 subplots of 100m2 each (with 3 subplots per one sector of 1/4ha, randomly delimited). The sampling effort thus corresponds to 0.12 ha. Right now (2021-2023), we are enlarging the sampling effort to one full 1/4ha, plus the subplots of the others 1/4ha. After that, each site will then have 0.34 ha of permanent plots. All individuals >= 5cm of dbh are tagged and have been monitored for at least two censuses. Inside of each subplot of 100m2, we still have 4 subplots of 10m2 each to sample juveniles (>=1 cm to <=5 cm of dbh), totalizing 480m2 per site. Juveniles are also tagged and have been monitored for at least two censuses. One site (FNC-01; Flona Chapecó) with permanent plot has another sampling design: it has 24 plots of 50x10 m, and all individuals with at least 9.5cm dbh are tagged, with three censuses.
Network.Standardized.Spatial.Structure.D: Phillips et. Al, 2016.Manual de Campo para o Estabelecimento e Remedição de Parcelas. Rainfor.org

Network.Objectives: The main purpose of this monitoring network is to analyze the relationships between ES and land management practices, and therefore to utilize this research as a tool for advancing sustainable land management practices and policies throughout the region. PEBANPA monitors natural ecosystems of South Patagonia (Argentina), and produce scientific research focused on ecosystem function and ecosystem services, as well as on trends in biodiversity and the interactions between natural environments and land-use activities.

Network.Funding: Federal, State or Local government funds | Research funds
Network.Standard.Spatial.Structure: Plots in PEBANPA are geo-referenced, permanent and semi-permanent. These encompass native forests, grasslands, shrublands, and wetlands across environmental gradients in the provinces of Santa Cruz and Tierra del Fuego, Argentina, reflecting the full longitudinal and latitudinal gradients of ecosystems, temperature, rainfall and land-use intensities. At each sampling location, variables have been measured in an approximately 20 m × 50 m quadrat (1000 m2).

Network.Objectives: Biodiversity (trees, birds, medium and large mammals and butterflies) and integrated environmental monitoring. The LTER site in Roraima monitors sites previously established by the Biodiversity Research Program (PPBio / MCTI) and Kamukaia Network (Embrapa) in understudied forest vegetation types in the Amazon (ie, seasonal white sand forests) and in forest areas managed by local communities for non-timber forest products (Brazil nut). Network.Standard.Spatial.Structure:
La aproximación para el estudio de las cimas se realiza siguiendo un protocolo de campo estandarizado. Cada sitio piloto GLORIA comprende tres o cuatro cimas a diferentes altitudes, por encima de la línea de bosques hasta el límite de la vida vegetal vascular. 
En cada cumbre se mide composición y cobertura de vegetación y cobertura de sustratos a nivel de secciones cimeras y en cuadrantes de 1m2.
Cada cima se divide en ocho secciones, a 5 y 10 m de desnivel del punto cumbral (HSP) y en los cuatro puntos cardinales. En cada orientación, a los 5 m del HSP, se establece un clúster de 3 x 3m, en cuyos vértices se instalan cuatro cuadrantes de 1×1 m y en el centro, el sensor/logger de temperatura.

Network.Name: Programa de Pesquisa em Biodiversidade da Amazônia Ocidental
Network.Institution.Name: na
Network.Admin.Name: na
Network.Objectives: Biodiversity (trees, birds, medium and large mammals and butterflies) and integrated environmental monitoring. The LTER site in Roraima monitors sites previously established by the Biodiversity Research Program (PPBio / MCTI) and Kamukaia Network (Embrapa) in understudied forest vegetation types in the Amazon (ie, seasonal white sand forests) and in forest areas managed by local communities for non-timber forest products (Brazil nut). Long-term monitoring is oriented towards the joint understanding of the effects of environmental determinants (soil texture and fertility, topography, water table depth) and climate variation within and between years in the biota (trees, birds, medium and large mammals size and butterflies) and on the functioning of the forest (carbon stocks, carbon -COD- transport between vegetation, water and soil, and leaf decomposition).
Network.Target: na
Network.Standard.Spatial.Structure: The PELD FORR uses two different standard sampling arraies: (i) a 25 km2 grid system with 30 1-ha permanent plots systematucally distributed  (RAPELD method) and (ii) 9 hectares permanent plots (300 m x 300 m) established in  Brazilian nut tree groves ("castanhais").
Network.Standardized.Spatial.Structure.D: Magnusson et al. 2005. RAPELD: a modification of the Gentry method for biodiversity surveys in long-term ecological research sites. Biota Neotrop 5: 1–6.

Network.Objectives: RLS represents a unique collaboration between professional & citizen scientists, with a joint mission to INFORM managers and the broader community.
